nodes.title: Frobenius twists are contracting for large powers
nodes.statement: Let c : C → X × X be a correspondence over 𝔽̄_q defined over 𝔽_q. (a) If Z ⊂ X is closed, n satisfies qⁿ > ram(c₂, Z), and Z is c^{(n)}-invariant, then c^{(n)} is contracting near Z. (b) If Z is a closed locally c-invariant subset defined over 𝔽_q, then c^{(n)} is contracting near Z in a neighbourhood of fixed points for every n with qⁿ > ram(c₂, Z). (c) If c₂ is quasi-finite, then for every n with qⁿ > ram(c₂), c^{(n)} is contracting near every closed point in a neighbourhood of fixed points, and Fix(c^{(n)}) is finite.
hypotheses: k = 𝔽̄_q; c defined over 𝔽_q; ram as in EDC.8/contracting-correspondence.
proofSteps: (a): with d = ram(c₂, Z), (c₁^{(n)})·(I_Z) is the qⁿ-th power of an ideal contained in I_{c₂^{−1}(Z)_red}, hence inside I_{c₂^{−1}(Z)_red}^{d+1} ⊂ I_{c₂^{−1}(Z)}, and its d-th power lies in I_{c₂^{−1}(Z)}^{d+1} (Varshavsky Lemma 2.2.3).

(b): a locally c-invariant Z defined over 𝔽_q is locally c^{(n)}-invariant, so it is c^{(n)}|_W-invariant on the open W(Z) ⊃ Fix(c^{(n)}) (EDC.8/correspondence-pullback-and-restriction); apply (a) to c|_W (Varshavsky Corollary 2.2.4(a)).

(c): closed points are locally invariant when c₂ is quasi-finite (Varshavsky Example 1.5.2, Corollary 2.2.4(b)); finiteness of Fix by EDC.8/contracting-local-terms (a) applied at each point (Theorem 2.3.2(a)).
acceptance: For c the identity correspondence of X₀ ⊗ 𝔽̄_q, c^{(n)} is the graph of Frobenius^n, whose fixed points are X₀(𝔽_{qⁿ}), finite, for every n ≥ 1 (ram = 1).

sources.locator: Lemma 2.2.3, Corollary 2.2.4, pp. 19; Theorem 2.3.2(a), p. 20 (arXiv v2)
sources.match: Twisting a correspondence defined over 𝔽_q by a large power of Frobenius makes it contracting near invariant subsets and near closed points, and makes the fixed-point set finite.

nodes.title: The Fujiwara–Varshavsky trace formula (Deligne’s conjecture)
nodes.statement: Let c : C → X × X be a correspondence over 𝔽̄_q defined over 𝔽_q, and U ⊂ X an open subset defined over 𝔽_q such that the restriction c₁:c₁^{−1}(U)→U is proper, c₂ is quasi-finite over c₂^{−1}(U), and X ∖ U is locally c-invariant. Then there is d ≥ ram(c₂|_{c₂^{−1}(U)}) such that for every F ∈ D^b_ctf(X, Λ) with F|_{X∖U} = 0, every n with qⁿ > d and every c^{(n)}-morphism u : c₂!(c₁^{(n)})^*F → F: Tr(RΓ_c(u)) = Σ_{y ∈ Fix(c^{(n)}) ∩ c₂^{−1}(U)} Tr(u_y | F_{c₂(y)}), a finite sum of naive local terms. If X and C are proper, d := max{ram(c₂|_{c₂^{−1}(U)}), ram(c₂, X ∖ U)} works. For F with a Weil structure ψ : Fr^*F → F and a c-morphism u, u^{(n)} := u ∘ ψⁿ is a c^{(n)}-morphism, and for U = X this is Deligne's conjecture proved by Fujiwara.
hypotheses: k = 𝔽̄_q; c and U defined over 𝔽_q; the properness/quasi-finiteness over U and local invariance of X ∖ U; Λ and D^b_ctf as in EDC.8/scheme-correspondence's setting; RΓ_c(u) as in Varshavsky 2.3.1 (defined using c₁ proper over U and F|_{X∖U} = 0).
proofSteps: Restrict to c₁⁻¹U and use properness of c₁:c₁⁻¹U→U to construct RΓ_c(u); the assumption F|_(X∖U)=0 identifies RΓ_c(U,F|_U) with RΓ_c(X,F). This is Varshavsky 2.3.1.

Reduce (b) to (c): restrict to c₁^{−1}(U), compactify so that X̄ ∖ U stays locally invariant (Varshavsky Lemma 1.5.4), and extend u by zero; traces are unchanged (EDC.8/cohomological-correspondence-pushforward).

(c): by EDC.8/lefschetz-verdier-trace-formula, Tr(RΓ_c(u)) = Σ_β LT_β(u). Components with c₂(β) ⊂ X ∖ U: c^{(n)} contracts near X ∖ U (EDC.8/frobenius-twist-contracting (b)), so LT_β(u) = LT_β(u|_{X∖U}) = 0 as F|_{X∖U} = 0 (EDC.8/contracting-local-terms).

Components meeting c₂^{−1}(U) are points y (EDC.8/frobenius-twist-contracting (c)), c^{(n)} contracts near c₂(y), and LT_y(u) = LT_y(u|_x) = Tr(u_y) (EDC.8/contracting-local-terms and the naive term of EDC.8/correspondence-pullback-and-restriction (d)) (Varshavsky Theorem 2.3.2, Remark 2.3.3).
acceptance: For c the identity correspondence of X₀ ⊗ 𝔽̄_q with X₀ proper, U = X and u^{(n)} = ψⁿ the Weil structure: the formula is the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula Tr(Frⁿ | RΓ(X, F)) = Σ_{x ∈ X₀(𝔽_{qⁿ})} Tr(Frⁿ_x | F_x), the theorem of CohomologicalPointCounting TraceFormula Layer 11, here recovered for all n ≥ 1 (ram = 1).

For a Hecke correspondence of a compactified modular curve with U the open modular curve, the formula computes Tr(Frobⁿ ∘ T | H_c) by fixed points in U for n large, the input consumed by EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.5 and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.1a.

sources.match: Varshavsky's generalisation of Fujiwara's theorem: for qⁿ large, the trace of a Frobenius-twisted correspondence on compactly supported cohomology is the sum of naive local terms over fixed points in U; for U = X it is Deligne's conjecture proved by Fujiwara.

nodes.title: Naive local terms under a punctured-cone hypothesis and for tame finite-order automorphisms
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed and X separated of finite type over k. (a) If f:X→X fixes x and N_x(f) has no nonzero fixed points, then x is isolated and LT_x(u)=Tr(u_x|F_x) for any u:f*F→F with F constructible of finite Tor dimension. (b) If X is smooth at an isolated fixed point x of a semisimple element g of a linear algebraic group acting on X, the normal-cone hypothesis holds and the same equality follows. (c) For an automorphism g of finite order invertible in k, the equality holds at every isolated fixed point, including singular ones, by applying the trace comparison to the full fixed subscheme Z=Fix(g). If X is proper and X^g has finite support, its global trace is the sum of their stalk traces. The arbitrary singular semisimple-group application remains an unverified target in this review. The cone of the reduced point can have nonzero fixed points even in (c); it is not an asserted intermediate result. The perfect-scheme transport is a separate Part II target.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
k algebraically closed; for (c), g^m = id as k-scheme automorphisms with m invertible in k, so that ⟨g⟩ is a finite diagonalizable group of order prime to p.

Only (b) requires smoothness at x. In (c) use the full fixed subscheme, not the reduced point. The smooth fixed-locus/tangent identification for the diagonalizable closure of ⟨g⟩ is an explicit SF.0 request; no general fixed-scheme/normal-cone comparison is assumed.
proofSteps: (a) Apply the proper-component part of normal-cone-trace-comparison with Z={x}; its restricted trace is the stalk trace.

(b) For the diagonalizable closure D of ⟨g⟩, the fixed locus of smooth X is smooth at x and its tangent space is (T_xX)^D. An isolated fixed point has zero fixed tangent space. Since N_xX=T_xX when X is smooth, the cone condition follows. This uses the precise smooth fixed-locus input requested from SF.0, not the false general Lemma 5.1.

(c) Use the tame-fixed-subscheme-normal-cone theorem with the full scheme Z=Fix(g), which gives NoAlmostTubularFixed without smoothness. Apply normal-cone-trace-comparison to Z. An isolated component β of Z has finite nonreduced support, is proper over k, and has the same étale site as its reduced point. The restricted graph is the identity correspondence because g|Z=id. Thus its local term is the stalk trace. For the global statement sum these terms in the proper Lefschetz–Verdier formula. The arbitrary singular semisimple-group target still needs either a valid local equivariant affine argument or a different proof.
acceptance: For the involution x ↦ −x of ℙ¹ (p ≠ 2) with F = Λ, u = id: fixed points 0 and ∞, naive terms 1 + 1 = 2 = Tr(g^* | H⁰ ⊕ H²) = 1 + 1.

The finite-order hypothesis matters: for translation by 1 on 𝔸¹ ⊂ ℙ¹ in characteristic p (order p, not prime to p), the unique fixed point ∞ has naive term 1 while Tr(g^* | H*(ℙ¹)) = 2, so the local term at ∞ is 2, not naive.

On Spec k[x,y,z]/(x³+yz) with g=(x,−y,−z), char k≠2, the origin is isolated in X^g but N_0X=Spec k[x,y,z]/(yz) has a fixed line. NoTubularFixed fails; tame order and isolated support alone are insufficient. This is a counterexample to the omitted normal-cone implication, without determining its true local term.

nodes.title: Characteristic polynomials of the two sides of a similitude are reciprocal
nodes.statement: Let F be a field, V and W vector spaces of the same finite dimension b over F, ⟨·,·⟩ : V × W → F a perfect pairing, c ∈ F^×, and φ ∈ GL(V), ψ ∈ GL(W) with ⟨φv, ψw⟩ = c⟨v, w⟩ for all v, w. Then, under W ≅ V^∨ given by the pairing, ψ = c·(φ^∨)^{−1}; consequently det(ψ) = c^b det(φ)^{−1} and, in F[t], det(1 − tψ | W) = det(φ)^{−1}·det(φ − ct | V); equivalently, in F(t), det(1 − tψ | W) = (−ct)^b·det(φ)^{−1}·det(1 − (ct)^{−1}φ | V). Over an algebraic closure, the eigenvalues of ψ with algebraic multiplicity are the c/α for α the eigenvalues of φ. No semisimplicity of φ or ψ is assumed.
hypotheses: F any field; ⟨·,·⟩ perfect; φ, ψ invertible; similitude factor c ∈ F^× (the same on both sides).
proofSteps: ⟨v, ψw⟩ = c⟨φ^{−1}v, w⟩, so the functional ⟨·, ψw⟩ equals c·⟨·, w⟩ ∘ φ^{−1}; i.e. ψ corresponds to c·(φ^{−1})^∨ = c·(φ^∨)^{−1}.
det(1 − tψ) = det(1 − tc·(φ^∨)^{−1}) = det(1 − tc·φ^{−1}) (transpose invariance, mathlib:Matrix.charpoly_transpose / mathlib:LinearMap.det_dualMap) = det(φ)^{−1} det(φ − ct).

Taking t = 0 in det(ψ − x) form, or comparing constant terms, gives det ψ = c^b det(φ)^{−1}; the eigenvalue statement is the root statement for det(φ − ct) (compare mathlib:Matrix.charpoly_inv for c = 1).
acceptance: b = 1, V = W = F with ⟨v, w⟩ = vw, φ = α, ψ = c/α: det(1 − tψ) = 1 − (c/α)t and det(φ)^{−1}det(φ − ct) = (α − ct)/α.
A unipotent φ (Jordan block, α = 1) with c = q gives ψ with the single eigenvalue q of the same algebraic multiplicity, without diagonalisability.

nodes.title: The determinant of a similitude of a symmetric or alternating form
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, V of finite dimension b with a perfect bilinear form ⟨·,·⟩ which is symmetric (ε = +1) or alternating (ε = −1), c ∈ F^×, and φ ∈ GL(V) with ⟨φv, φw⟩ = c⟨v, w⟩. Fix s ∈ F̄ with s² = c and let m_± be the algebraic multiplicity of ±s as an eigenvalue of φ (the dimension of the generalized eigenspace over F̄). Then: (a) generalized eigenspaces V_α, V_β (α, β ∈ F̄) are orthogonal unless αβ = c, and V_α, V_{c/α} have equal dimension; (b) det(φ)² = c^b; (c) if ε = −1, then b, m_+ and m_− are even and det(φ) = c^{b/2}; (d) if ε = +1, then m_+ + m_− ≡ b (mod 2) and det(φ) = (−1)^{m_−} s^b, thus det(φ)=(−1)^{b−m_+}s^b as well. If b is even, s^b=c^{b/2}, and only then this simplifies to det(φ)=(−1)^{m_−}c^{b/2}. In odd rank retain s^b, even when s lies in F. For c=q^d with d even use s=q^{d/2}, so s^b=q^{(d/2)·b}, with no parity assumption on b.
hypotheses: char F ≠ 2; form perfect and ε-symmetric; φ a similitude with factor c; no semisimplicity of φ.
proofSteps: Extend scalars to an algebraic closure. Mathlib’s iSup_maxGenEigenspace_eq_top supplies the spanning primary spaces, and finrank_maxGenEigenspace_eq identifies their dimensions with charpoly.rootMultiplicity. Distinct primary spaces are independent by the coprime-polynomial kernel decomposition; the subsequent form argument uses these generalized spaces, not ordinary eigenspaces.

(a): write φ = α + N on V_α and φ = β + N′ on V_β with N, N′ nilpotent; then (c − αβ)⟨v, w⟩ = α⟨v, N′w⟩ + β⟨Nv, w⟩ + ⟨Nv, N′w⟩, and induction on the nilpotency orders gives ⟨v, w⟩ = 0 when αβ ≠ c; perfectness then pairs V_α perfectly with V_{c/α}.
(b) is EDC.8/similitude-charpoly-reciprocity with W = V, ψ = φ: det φ = c^b det(φ)^{−1}.
Eigenvalues α ≠ ±s come in pairs {α, c/α} of equal multiplicity, each pair contributing c^{dim V_α}; so det φ = c^{(b − m_+ − m_−)/2} s^{m_+} (−s)^{m_−} = (−1)^{m_−} s^b, and b − m_+ − m_− is even.

(c): V_s and V_{−s} are self-paired, so the alternating form restricts to perfect alternating forms on them: m_± even and det φ = s^b = c^{b/2} (b even for an alternating perfect form; Tau Ceti's rank-two case is LinearMap.det_eq_of_compl₁₂_self_eq_smul). Even rank of a perfect alternating space follows by choosing x,y with nonzero pairing, splitting off their nondegenerate two-dimensional plane and inducting on its orthogonal complement. Apply this to V, V_s and V_(−s); this supplies the evenness rather than presuming it from the rank-two determinant citation.
acceptance: Rank-two alternating case: det φ = c, matching tauceti:LinearMap.det_eq_of_compl₁₂_self_eq_smul.
Symmetric rank one with ⟨x, y⟩ = xy and φ = −s (c = s²): m_− = 1 and det φ = −s, so the sign is not determined by the form alone.
Isometries (c = 1): det(φ)² = 1, matching tauceti:TauCeti.BilinForm.IsIsometry.det_sq_mul_det_toMatrix_self.

sources.match: For n odd the middle form is alternating so b_n is even; for n even the sign of the functional equation is (−1)^N with N the dimension of the generalized eigenspace of q^{n/2}.
The sign of the functional equation is + if d is odd or q^{d/2} occurs an even number of times as an eigenvalue on H^d, and − otherwise.

nodes.title: Graded Frobenius duality data of weight (2d, q^d)
nodes.statement: Fix a field E of characteristic 0, an integer d ≥ 0 and q ∈ E^×. A graded Frobenius duality datum consists of finite-dimensional E-vector spaces H^i (0 ≤ i ≤ 2d; zero otherwise), automorphisms F_i ∈ GL(H^i), and perfect pairings ⟨·,·⟩_i : H^i × H^{2d−i} → E such that ⟨F_i x, F_{2d−i} y⟩_i = q^d ⟨x, y⟩_i and ⟨x, y⟩_i = (−1)^i ⟨y, x⟩_{2d−i} (the Koszul sign (−1)^{i(2d−i)} = (−1)^i of graded commutativity). Its Betti numbers are b_i := dim H^i, its Euler characteristic χ := Σ (−1)^i b_i, its polynomials P_i(t) := det(1 − tF_i | H^i) and its determinant Δ := ∏_i det(F_i)^{(−1)^i} ∈ E^×. The middle form ⟨·,·⟩_d is (−1)^d-symmetric.
hypotheses: E of characteristic 0 (so ℚ_ℓ with ℓ = 2 is allowed, and alternating and symmetric are distinct); pairings perfect; F acts by a similitude of factor q^d; no semisimplicity of F.
proofSteps: The data are linear algebra; the main instance is built from EDC.2's Poincaré duality: for X₀ smooth proper of pure dimension d over 𝔽_q and ℓ ∤ q, H^i := H^i(X, ℚ_ℓ), F_i := geometric Frobenius, ⟨x, y⟩_i := Tr(x ∪ y) with the trace H^{2d}(X, ℚ_ℓ) → ℚ_ℓ(−d) composed with the identification of ℚ_ℓ(−d) on which F acts by q^d (EDC.2:pairings/cup-product-trace-pairing, EDC.2:pairings/galois-frobenius-equivariance, EDC.2:pairings/adic-and-rational-poincare-duality).
Graded commutativity of cup product gives the Koszul sign; equivariance of the trace under Frobenius gives the similitude factor q^d (Weil I (2.5)).

A second instance: X₀ proper of pure dimension d whose dualizing complex has a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism a^!ℚ_ℓ ≅ ℚ_ℓ(d)[2d] (a rational homology manifold), with the pairing from EDC.1:biduality/relative-and-geometric-duality; this is the datum WeilConjectures:WC.6/homology-manifold-weil-assembly needs.
acceptance: ℙ¹ over 𝔽_q: H⁰ = E with F = 1, H² = E with F = q, ⟨1, 1⟩ = 1; d = 1, χ = 2, Δ = q.
A smooth projective curve of genus g: H¹ of dimension 2g with the alternating cup-product form and F a symplectic similitude of factor q.

nodes.title: Reciprocity of Frobenius polynomials and the determinant relation
nodes.statement: For a graded Frobenius duality datum (EDC.8/graded-frobenius-duality-datum) of weight (2d, q^d): (a) b_i = b_{2d−i}; (b) for 0 ≤ i ≤ 2d, P_{2d−i}(t)·det(F_i) = (−q^d t)^{b_i}·P_i(1/(q^d t)) as an identity in E(t), and the eigenvalues of F_{2d−i} with algebraic multiplicity are the q^d/α for α those of F_i; (c) det(F_i)·det(F_{2d−i}) = q^{d b_i}; (d) if d is odd, b_d is even and det(F_d) = q^{d b_d/2}; if d is even, det(F_d) = (−1)^{m_−} q^{(d/2)·b_d} = (−1)^{b_d − m_+} q^{(d/2)·b_d}, where m_± is the algebraic multiplicity of ±q^{d/2} as an eigenvalue of F_d; (e) Δ² = q^{dχ}, and dχ is even. These are statements about the actual finite-dimensional spaces; no semisimplicity of Frobenius is assumed, and no zeta function is defined here (WeilConjectures:WC.2 assembles the signed functional equation from them). For X₀ smooth proper over 𝔽_q of pure dimension d and E = ℚ_ℓ (ℓ ∤ q, ℓ = 2 allowed) these apply to H^i(X, ℚ_ℓ) with geometric Frobenius, and likewise for proper rational homology manifolds.
hypotheses: A graded Frobenius duality datum over a field of characteristic 0; for the geometric instances, the hypotheses of EDC.2:pairings (smooth proper) or a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism a^!ℚ_ℓ ≅ ℚ_ℓ(d)[2d] (homology manifold).
For odd d the exponent d·b_d/2 is an integer because b_d is even. For even d use (d/2)·b_d; writing d·(b_d/2) would be incorrect when b_d is odd.
proofSteps: (a): the pairing H^i × H^{2d−i} → E is perfect.

(b), (c): apply EDC.8/similitude-charpoly-reciprocity to V = H^i, W = H^{2d−i}, φ = F_i, ψ = F_{2d−i}, c = q^d: det(1 − tF_{2d−i}) = det(F_i)^{−1} det(F_i − q^d t), and det(F_i − q^d t) = (−q^d t)^{b_i} det(1 − (q^d t)^{−1}F_i).
(d): the middle form is (−1)^d-symmetric (Koszul sign); apply EDC.8/form-similitude-determinant with c = q^d and s = q^{d/2} when d is even.

(e): pairing i with 2d − i (same parity), Δ² = ∏_i (det F_i · det F_{2d−i})^{(−1)^i} = ∏_i q^{d b_i (−1)^i} = q^{dχ}; dχ is even because d even, or d odd and χ ≡ b_d ≡ 0 mod 2 after pairing the other degrees.
acceptance: ℙ¹: P₂(t)·det(F₀) = 1 − qt = (−qt)·(1 − 1/(qt)) = (−qt)·P₀(1/(qt)); Δ = q, χ = 2, Δ² = q².
A curve of genus g: det(F₁) = q^g (alternating middle form), Δ = 1 · q^{−g} · q = q^{1−g}, χ = 2 − 2g and Δ² = q^{2−2g} = q^{dχ}.

A smooth quadric surface over 𝔽_q (d = 2) whose two rulings are swapped by Frobenius: F on H² = ℚ_ℓ(−1)² has eigenvalues q and −q, m_− = 1, so det(F₂) = −q², the sign that the split quadric (eigenvalue q twice) does not have.

nodes.title: Fixed-point conditions in a punctured tubular neighbourhood
nodes.statement: For a self-correspondence c:C→X×X and closed Z⊂X, let N_Z(c):N_(c⁻¹(Z×Z))C→N_ZX×N_ZX be the induced conical correspondence and let V=Fix(c|Z) be its vertex. Define NoTubularFixed(c,Z) by |Fix(N_Z(c))|∖|V|=∅. Define NoAlmostTubularFixed(c,Z) by NoTubularFixed together with finiteness of {t∈k : |Fix((t·N_Z(c)₁,N_Z(c)₂))|∖|V|≠∅}. In the comparison theorem Z is schematically c-invariant: c₂⁻¹Z⊆c₁⁻¹Z, equivalently c₂⁻¹Z=c⁻¹(Z×Z). This is stronger than invariance only of underlying sets.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
Use scheme inverse images and relative normal cones; the two fixed-point predicates compare underlying sets. Scalar t=0 is included.
proofSteps: Functoriality of relative normal cones defines both legs and their common vertex. The scalar action on the first leg defines the family.
The inclusion N_(Fix(c|Z))Fix(c)↪Fix(N_Z(c)) and Nakayama show that NoTubularFixed makes Fix(c|Z) an open and closed part of Fix(c) after reduction (Lemma 4.8).

For a contracting correspondence restricted to a neighbourhood of its fixed points, the first cone leg has set-theoretic image in the vertex. Every scalar then has empty punctured fixed locus (Lemma 4.7).
acceptance: For graph x↦λx on 𝔸¹, Z={0}, λ∈k×∖{1}, NoTubularFixed holds and the bad-scalar set is {λ⁻¹}.
For the identity of 𝔸¹ at Z={0}, NoTubularFixed fails.

nodes.title: Constancy of relative traces for universally locally acyclic coefficients
nodes.statement: Let S be connected, c:C→X×_S X a relative correspondence, and u:c₁*F→c₂!F a relative cohomological correspondence. Assume F is universally locally acyclic over S and Fix(c)→S is topologically constant: Fix(c)_red≅Y×S_red over S for some Y. For any geometric points s,t of S, the canonical identification H⁰(Fix(c_s),K_Fix(c_s))≅H⁰(Fix(c_t),K_Fix(c_t)) takes Tr(c_s,u_s) to Tr(c_t,u_t). The groups belong to the fixed-point fibres, not to X_s and X_t.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
S is connected; the topological trivialization is over S; use relative extraordinary pullback and the fibre restriction of u. F is ULA, not merely lisse on a single fibre.
proofSteps: Reduce equality between geometric fibres to specialization on strict henselian traits using constructibility and connectedness.
ULA gives F_s≅Ψ(F_η̄), compatible with every base change. The nearby-cycle exchange maps carry the relative correspondence to its specialized one.

Trace commutes with this specialization by the product-duality and evaluation diagrams of §7. The topologically constant fixed-point family identifies its dualizing cohomology, so specializing its trace does not change the element.
acceptance: For X=Y×S,F=pr_Y*G and the product of one fixed correspondence with S, all fibre traces agree.
ULA cannot be dropped: take X=S=𝔸¹ with the relative identity correspondence and F the skyscraper at 0. The fixed family is topologically constant, but the fibre traces are 1 at 0 and 0 away from 0.

nodes.title: Trace comparison with an invariant closed subscheme
nodes.statement: Let c:C→X×X and let Z⊂X be a schematically c-invariant closed subscheme. Assume NoTubularFixed(c,Z). Then Fix(c|Z)_red is open and closed in Fix(c)_red. (a) If also NoAlmostTubularFixed(c,Z), restriction of Tr_c(u) to Fix(c|Z) equals Tr_(c|Z)(u|Z) for every c-morphism u on a constructible finite-Tor complex. (b) Every connected component β of Fix(c|Z) that is proper over k is a connected component of Fix(c), and LT_β(u)=LT_β(u|Z). Part (b) requires no global NoAlmostTubularFixed assumption.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
Schematic invariance and the punctured-cone conditions are those of the dedicated definition node; in (b) β is proper, although X and C need not be proper.
proofSteps: Use closed/open trace additivity to reduce to F|Z=0. Specialize c,u,F to the normal cone. The fixed family near the vertex is topologically constant, and the trace-specialization exchange identifies its trace with the original restriction.

Verdier’s zero-section theorem gives sp_ZF|Z=0, while monodromicity of specialization allows a finite power of the scaling action to give weak equivariance at finite coefficients. This is Verdier SP1 and Proposition 5.1; the adic passage must use normalized finite-level limits, not an assumed global equivariant structure.

The zero stalk along the vertex extends the weak equivariance across scalar 0. Remove the finitely many bad nonzero scalars and retain 0 and 1. On this scalar family F⊠Λ is ULA; relative trace constancy identifies the trace at 1 with the zero trace at 0. This proves (a).

For (b) first isolate the proper component β. The quotient of the punctured fixed cone by 𝔾_m is proper over β. Its projection to the scalar line has closed image disjoint from 0, hence a finite image. This is Lemma 3.9 and gives the required local no-almost condition; apply (a) and integrate the trace over β.
acceptance: A graph x↦λx, λ≠1 on 𝔸¹ at Z={0}, has local term equal to its stalk trace.
For contracting correspondences the no-almost predicate holds with no bad scalars and recovers the 2007 comparison.
For Z=X the restriction identity is tautological; removing properness of β does not leave a scalar-valued local term.

nodes.title: Sublinear negative cohomology in étale towers
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, ℓ invertible in k, X=∏_{a=1}^n X_a with X_a smooth projective connected curves, and f:U→X quasi-finite separated. For K∈pD≥0(U,ℚ̄_ℓ) there is C independent of connected finite étale covers X̃_a→X_a of degrees d_a such that, for Ũ=U×_X∏X̃_a, dim H^i(Ũ,K)≤C∏d_a for all i, and for i<0 it is bounded by C·max_{|A|=n−|i|}∏_{a∈A}d_a (zero if |i|>n). Consequently, for any perverse sheaf F on a finite-type k-scheme and point x there is an affine étale neighbourhood U and finite étale covers U_N→U of degrees e_N→∞ with dim H^i(U_N,F)=o(e_N) for every i<0.
hypotheses: The pullback of K to each cover is understood. The product bound is for n≥1; the zero-dimensional case is immediate. The constant depends on K and f, never on the covers.
proofSteps: Reduce the projective-product upper-perverse bound to sheaves shifted by support dimension and to finite coefficients via universal coefficients. Induct on the number of factors.

On a dense open of the first curve the relevant direct images are lisse. Leray, Euler–Poincaré with Swan conductors, and induction control ranks. Nearby-cycle perverse bounds control the Swan contributions by the same smaller products. Duality gives the lower-perverse bound; quasi-finite f_* preserves pD≥0, giving 4.5.4.

Choose a quasi-finite affine-space map near x, and an étale neighbourhood pulled back from a product of positive-genus projective curves. Covers of each curve with degree d→∞ give total degree d^n while each negative-degree bound is O(d^(n−|i|)). This yields the sublinear conclusion used in 5.2.3–5.2.8.
acceptance: For a positive-genus smooth projective curve C, F=ℚ̄_ℓ[1], dim H⁻¹(C̃,F)=1 while the cover degree tends to infinity.
For n=2 and i=−1 the bound is C·max(d₁,d₂), rather than C·d₁d₂; equal-degree towers distinguish these rates.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.5.1 and Corollaries 4.5.3–4.5.5, pp.117–121; use in 5.2.3–5.2.8, pp.131–134
sources.match: Product-cover estimates, their quasi-finite form and the sublinear negative-cohomology tower required by the higher-dimensional weight criterion.

nodes.title: The full fixed subscheme has no punctured-cone fixed points for a tame automorphism
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, X separated of finite type over k, and g an automorphism with g^m=id for a positive m invertible in k. Set Z=Fix(g) as the full scheme equalizer, including nilpotents. Then Fix(N_Z(g))=Z as schemes. The graph (g,id) has no almost fixed points in the punctured tubular neighbourhood of Z: its bad-scalar set is contained in {λ⁻¹ : λ^m=1, λ≠1}. Neither smoothness of X nor reducedness of Z is required. This statement does not replace Z by Z_red.
hypotheses: Use the full scheme fixed locus and its ideal; the tame finite-order assumption allows spectral projectors for the m distinct roots of unity. X is separated, so fixed points have finite-group invariant affine neighbourhoods.
proofSteps: Near any point of Z choose an affine open U containing that fixed point. The intersection of the finitely many g^iU is affine because X is separated, contains the point, and is g-invariant. Work on X=Spec A there.

Write A=⊕_{λ^m=1} A_λ using the explicit spectral projectors (1/m)Σ_j λ^(−j)g^j, also for infinite-dimensional A over k. The fixed ideal I is generated by A_λ for λ≠1, since it is generated by g(a)−a. The quotient Q=A/I has trivial g-action.

The Q-module I/I² is generated by images of the nontrivial A_λ. Since Q has trivial action and the spectral projectors are exact, (I/I²)_1=0. The graded Q-algebra gr_I A is generated in degree one via Sym_Q(I/I²)↠gr_I A. In the fixed-scheme quotient all degree-one generators are killed, so only degree-zero Q remains. Hence Fix(N_Z(g))=Spec Q, including its nilpotents.

For the scalar-twisted cone map the action on a degree-one λ-generator is tλ. Outside the finite set λ⁻¹ with λ≠1, all degree-one generators are again killed in the fixed quotient. The set omits 0 and 1. These local computations agree on overlaps and prove the no-almost predicate globally.
acceptance: For X=Spec k[x,y,z]/(x³+yz), g=(x,−y,−z), char k≠2, the full fixed ideal is (y,z), and Z=Spec k[x]/(x³). Its conormal generators have character −1, so its fixed cone is exactly this nonreduced Z. The cone along the reduced origin instead has a fixed line; replacing Z by Z_red would fail.
For the involution on 𝔸¹ the fixed subscheme is {0}; the only possible bad scalar is −1. For the identity, Z=X and the bad-scalar set is empty.

The result does not extend to order divisible by char k: for g(t)=t+1 on ℙ¹ in characteristic p, at ∞ the conormal character is trivial, so the spectral-projector step is unavailable and the local term can differ from its stalk trace.

gaps.title: Semisimplicity of the characteristic-zero decomposition over smaller coefficient fields
gaps.detail: BBD 6.2.5 is stated with ℂ (equivalently ℚ̄_ℓ) coefficients. For K defined over a subfield E ⊂ ℂ (for example ℚ) with K ⊗ ℂ semisimple of geometric origin, the vanishing of the degree-one connecting maps of the perverse truncation triangles descends to E because Hom spaces commute with coefficient extension, so Rf_*K ≅ ⊕ pH^i(Rf_*K)[−i] over E. Semisimplicity of the pH^i over E additionally needs Galois descent of subobjects of perverse sheaves along coefficient extension, which EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension (Hom ⊗ E′ compatibility) does not state. The node asserts the splitting over E and records semisimplicity over E as this gap.

sourceIssues.reason: Take char k≠2, X=𝔸², g(u,v)=(−u,−v), Z=V(uv). This is a reduced invariant Cartier divisor and D=µ₂ is reduced. N_ZX=Spec k[u,v,t]/(uv), with g(t)=t, so (N_ZX)^D=Spec k[t].
